title: FDA flags persistent data-integrity lapses, insanitary conditions at Indian drug facilities

contentHtml:
Mumbai: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) continues to find serious data-integrity violations at Indian pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities and clinical research organisations, making information they submit for regulatory assessment unacceptable, a senior agency official said.

Eight years after FDA issued guidelines on data integrity, its inspectors continue to find violations that require the affected studies or tests to be repeated for reliable data, Constance Richard-Math, the agency's deputy country director in India, told an industry gathering in Mumbai.

FDA's routine or unannounced inspections have also uncovered cases in which truckloads of key documents relating to analytical testing, manufacturing procedures and storage were discarded, including records destroyed using paper shredders, Richard-Math said. These violations, she warned, impedes building reliable and resilient supply chains.

FDA inspections continue to identify unacceptable and, in some cases, gross insanitary conditions in manufacturing facilities, she said, sharing pictures of dirty and dilapidated facilities.

Richard-Math urged drugmakers to look beyond their own facilities and scrutinise suppliers, vendors and other entities across the supply chain to ensure the safety of medicines.

"These may not be your facilities, but I would ask you to look beyond the walls of your own facilities: know your suppliers, know your vendors, know who is operating within your supply chain," she said.

"If you identify facilities operating at this level, whether they are vendors, contractors or even companies operating in your community, do not look the other way."
